known_limitations: G3-C13 is flaky at seed 0 (known, human decision of 27 Oct 2026). Here it failed once and passed once on the same seed, because bf16 GPU training is not deterministic.
C12 margin on mean_B_at_A is thin (0.125 against the < 0.2 limit), consistent with the reference sweep. The unconditioned model reached 0.235 (report only).
BaseModel built with config=None aliases the global mainConfig in hparams (legacy behaviour). Gate 3 decides conditioning from the network itself; class_table() still reads hparams.config.prepData.
An unconditioned model ignores apix in forward/predict_step: the output does not depend on it, and Gate 4 can pass it unconditionally.
Fine-tuning a conditioned checkpoint into an unconditioned model raises (unexpected cond.* keys). Scale conditioning cannot be dropped by fine-tuning.
val_loss_<class name> is logged only for batches where that class is available (batch_size = number of available samples), so classes never available in validation have no metric.
notes_for_next_agent: INFERENCE CALL PATTERN (Gate 4): model = InferenceModel.load_from_checkpoint(ckpt, strict=True) (v2 checkpoints load strictly, G3-C11). For each level from plan_levels: probs = model.predict_step(x, 0, apix=level.apix_work), with x [B,1,64,64,64] and apix a Python float or a [B,1] float32 tensor (a float is broadcast over the batch). This returns sigmoid(logits) [B,C,64,64,64], with channel c = class-table row c. Equivalently, logits = model(x, apix=level.apix_work). Passing apix to an unconditioned model is allowed and ignored. apix=None gives exactly the unconditioned computation, also for a conditioned model, so always pass apix to a conditioned model. CONDITIONING FLAG: use model.scale_conditioning(), which is True if the built network has the FiLM modules (model.model.cond). From a raw checkpoint config, use safe_getattr(cfg.train.network, 'scale_conditioning', False). CLASS TABLE: labels.multiclass.class_table_from_config(model.hparams.config.prepData), or model.class_table(). It is used only when model.is_pipeline_v2() (train.data_pipeline_version == 2); a v1 model has one channel (the legacy heatmap). len(table) == model.model.out.conv.conv.out_channels. CHECKPOINT KEYS ADDED: state_dict 'model.cond.scale_embed.mlp.{0,2}.{weight,bias}' and 'model.cond.film.{0..5}.lin.{weight,bias}' (only when scale_conditioning=True); 'model.out.conv.conv.{weight,bias}' has C output channels for v2. Config fields in hyper_parameters: train.network.scale_conditioning, train.particles (class_weights, loss_checkpoint; once the escalated TrainConfig field lands). Older checkpoints get the defaults through backfill_missing_fields. FiLM: t = log(apix/10), six FiLM points in the decoder (after encoder10, decoder5, decoder4, decoder3, decoder2, decoder1), zero-initialised. The Swin encoder and hidden_states_out[4] are unconditioned, so forward returns (logits, hidden4) for both models. TRAINING: v2 batches are recognised by the 'class_available'/'class_d_vox' keys and use multiclass_picking_loss. A conditioned model raises ValueError if 'apix_work' is missing. Fine-tune paths live in training/helpers._create_model: _fine_tune_into_v2 (legacy single-class -> copy out into every channel; v2 with another class table -> match channels by class number, new classes start from the mean; SSL -> the same). Resume compares (scale_conditioning, class table) of the checkpoint with the checkpoint config plus CLI changes, and raises ValueError on any difference.
